- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.7) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.4) — add 3–7% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast at 10% below peak if sentiment drops sharply post-spike.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3 consecutive forecasts are > 10% above true, adjust downward by 2–5% per period.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — dampen forecast volatility by 15–20% if sentiment swings > 0.3 in 3 days.
- Lagged sentiment: if sentiment peaks 2–3 days before forecast horizon, model should adjust downward by 2–5% to account for delayed market reaction.
